tool.name: yq
tool.description: Process YAML, JSON, XML, CSV, TSV, TOML and properties files
tool.command: yq #if $mode == "eval-all": ea #else: e #end if ## Null-input is automatically enabled when no input file is provided #if not $input_file: -n #end if #if str($sec_format.input_format) != "auto": -p '$sec_format.input_format' #end if #if str($sec_format.output_format) != "auto": -o '$sec_format.output_format' #end if #if $sec_format.pretty_print: -P #end if -I $sec_format.indent #if $sec_options.unwrap_scalar: -r #else: -r=false #end if #if $sec_options.no_doc_separators: -N #end if --security-disable-file-ops --security-disable-env-ops #if str($sec_options.front_matter) != "none": -f '$sec_options.front_matter' #end if ## Expression: from file or inline text (written to configfile to avoid sanitization/escaping issues) #if $expression_from_file: --from-file '$expression_from_file' #else: --from-file '$expr_file' #end if ## Input files (if any provided) #if $input_file: #for $f in $input_file: '$f' #end for #end if > '$output_file'

param.name: input_file
param.label: Input file(s)
param.help: The data file(s) to process. Multiple files can be selected (useful with eval-all mode to merge documents across files). When no file is provided, null-input mode (-n) is automatically enabled to create documents from scratch.

param.name: expression
param.label: Expression
param.help: The jq-like expression to evaluate (e.g. .a.b[0].c). Leave empty if loading the expression from a file.

param.name: expression_from_file
param.label: Expression from file
param.help: Load the expression from a file instead of typing it above. Overrides the expression text field.

param.name: mode
param.label: Mode
param.help: eval processes each document in each file in sequence; eval-all loads all documents of all files and runs the expression once.

param.name: input_format
param.label: Input format
param.help: Force the input format (default auto-detected from file extension).

param.name: pretty_print
param.label: Pretty print
param.help: Shorthand for pretty-printed output (indent style). Equivalent to ... style = ''

param.name: indent
param.label: Indent level
param.help: Number of spaces for indentation in the output (default 2).

param.name: unwrap_scalar
param.label: Unwrap scalars
param.help: Unwrap scalar values in the output (default true).

param.name: no_doc_separators
param.label: No document separators
param.help: Do not print --- document separators between YAML documents.

param.name: front_matter
param.label: Front matter
param.help: Extract or process YAML front matter (e.g. in Markdown files).

tool.help:
**What it does**
`yq` is a lightweight and portable command-line YAML, JSON, XML, CSV, TSV, TOML, HCL, INI and properties processor. It uses `jq`-like syntax but works with many file formats.
**Usage**
Provide a `jq`-like expression and an input file (or leave the input empty to create documents from scratch). `yq` will evaluate the expression and produce the output in the selected format.
When no input file is provided, null-input mode (`-n`) is automatically enabled so expressions can build new documents from scratch. Multiple input files can be selected; with eval-all mode, documents from all files are merged.
**Expression**
The expression uses `jq`-like syntax. Here are some quick examples:
- `.a.b[0].c` — navigate to `a`, then `b`, first element, then `c` - `.items[].name` — select the `name` field of each item in the `items` array - `.a.b.c = "value"` — set a value - `. as $item ireduce ({}; . * $item)` — merge multiple documents
**Examples**
- **Read a value**: Expression `.a.b[0]` on a YAML file returns the first element of `b` under `a`. - **Convert YAML to JSON**: Set output format to `json`. - **Convert JSON to YAML**: Set input format to `json` and output format to `yaml` with pretty print. - **Create from scratch**: Leave the input file empty and use expression `.a.b = "value"`. - **Merge files**: Select multiple files, use eval-all mode with `. as $item ireduce ({}; . * $item)`.
**Security**
For safety in Galaxy, file operations (`load()`, `load_base64()`, etc.) and environment variable access (`env`) are always disabled and cannot be turned off by the user.
**Documentation**
Full documentation: https://mikefarah.gitbook.io/yq/
